rounds.text: Tridhya Tech Ltd is heavily mispriced on an asset basis, trading at a price-to-book ratio of just 0.54x with a share price of ₹ 10.4 against a book value of ₹ 19.1 [E2]. This deep discount exists despite a robust 5-year compounded sales growth rate of 20% [E8]. Furthermore, the business is demonstrating a powerful operational turnaround, evidenced by a dramatic 132% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E13]. This massive earnings expansion has outpaced 1-year price growth by 174%, signaling that the company is beginning to outperform market expectations [E47]. Conceded: the 5-year and 3-year compounded profit growths stand at -12% and -43% respectively [E11, E12], along with low returns on capital and equity [E6, E7].

Tridhya Tech Ltd carries a severe fundamental disconnect between its lofty price-to-earnings multiple of 52.9 [E1] and its negligible capital efficiency, evidenced by an ROE of 1.0% [E7] and an ROCE of just 5.6% [E6]. This weak return profile is compounded by a catastrophic collapse in bottom-line performance over medium-term horizons, reflected in a 3-year compounded profit growth of -43% [E12] and a 5-year compounded profit growth of -12% [E11]. Furthermore, recent operational momentum has deteriorated sharply, marked by a drastic 48% year-over-year sales decline [E58] and persistent signals of decelerating earnings growth [E59], alongside a complete lack of shareholder returns via a 0.00% dividend yield [E4]. Conceded: the company demonstrates a 20% compounded sales growth over 5 years [E8] and a notable TTM profit growth rebound of 132% [E13], yet these positive metrics are heavily undercut by the stock languishing low in its 52-week range at just 26% of the way up [E5].

The bear's alarm over the 52.9 P/E multiple [E1] misses the foundational reality that the stock trades at an asset-backing discount with a price-to-book ratio of just 0.54x, valued at ₹ 10.4 against a book value of ₹ 19.1 [E2] for a micro-cap of ₹ 24.3 Cr [E3]. Conceded: the ROE sits at 1.0% [E7] and ROCE at 5.6% [E6], while medium-term profits show historical contractions of -12% over 5 years [E11] and -43% over 3 years [E12]. However, the bear overlooks the decisive inflection point where trailing twelve-month profit growth has violently rebounded by 132% [E13], vastly outpacing the sector median profit growth of 16.9% [E64]. This explosive bottom-line acceleration has triggered the scanX signal engine to note that profit growth exceeds 1-year price growth by 174%, proving the company is actively starting to outperform expectations [E47] even as it sits at 26% of its 52-week range [E5]. Finally, the criticism of zero dividends [E4] ignores that capital is being retained while the underlying business scales at a 20% compounded 5-year sales growth rate [E8].

Conceded: trailing twelve-month profit growth reached 132% [E13], outperforming the sector median profit growth of 16.9% [E64], and sales compounded at 20% over 5 years [E8]. However, citing an asset-backing discount of 0.54x price-to-book [E2] ignores that a business generating a meager 1.0% ROE [E7] and 5.6% ROCE [E6] destroys shareholder value on those assets, justifying the low valuation. The bull's reliance on recent profit acceleration masks severe ongoing deterioration, including a staggering 48% year-over-year sales decline [E58] and screens showing decelerating earnings growth [E59]. Furthermore, the historical profit contractions of -12% over 5 years [E11] and -43% over 3 years [E12] contextualize the 132% TTM bounce [E13] as a volatile recovery from a severely depressed base rather than a durable trend, while zero dividends [E4] leave investors uncompensated for holding a micro-cap [E3] sitting at just 26% of its 52-week range [E5].
